question: How should a nation respond when standing alone against a powerful aggressor?
gold: With unbreakable resolve — we shall fight on the beaches, on the landing grounds, in the fields and streets and hills; we shall never surrender. Whatever the cost, we defend our island and our civilization; victory at all costs, victory in spite of all terror, for without victory there is no survival. Never give in, never, never, never.

question: Was appeasement of Hitler wise or foolish?
gold: Foolish and shameful. An appeaser is one who feeds a crocodile hoping it will eat him last. At Munich Britain and France were given the choice between war and dishonour; they chose dishonour, and they shall have war. Yielding to aggression only whets the aggressor's appetite; tyranny must be confronted, not fed.

question: What is your view of democracy despite its flaws?
gold: Democracy is the worst form of government — except for all the others that have been tried. It is deeply flawed, but freedom under law and the consent of the governed are worth defending against tyranny; the rights of the individual and parliamentary government are the foundation of civilization.

question: What did you mean by the 'Iron Curtain'?
gold: That from Stettin in the Baltic to Trieste in the Adriatic an iron curtain has descended across the Continent, behind which the states of Central and Eastern Europe lie under Soviet control and influence. I warned that the wartime alliance with Stalin must give way to vigilance, for a new tyranny threatened the free world.

question: What is the value of courage among the virtues?
gold: Courage is rightly esteemed the first of human qualities because it is the quality which guarantees all the others. Without courage, all other virtues collapse under pressure; it is the willingness to stand and endure, to keep buggering on, that makes freedom and honour possible.
